# Comment on any page in Safari

For **Maya Lindqvist**, Reviewer; reads a colleague's HTML report or deck and says what she thinks. Designed.

## Goal
Maya comments on any web page from Safari, with nothing added to the page until she asks and nothing sent anywhere until she chooses, and gets the comments out the same ways as on a page with Pipeup built in.

## Steps

### Turn Pipeup on in Safari
![Turn Pipeup on in Safari](../../references/screens/jny-comment-in-safari/turn-on-in-safari--default--desktop--dark.png)

Wording (text the mock does not show as it is; `{…}` is what the data fills in):
- "Turn on Pipeup in Safari.": the line while Pipeup has never been on in Safari.
- "Under Extensions, tick Pipeup.": beneath it.
- "Pipeup is off in Safari.": the line once Pipeup was on and was turned off.
- "Under Extensions, tick Pipeup to turn it back on.": beneath it.
- "Pipeup is on in Safari.": the line while it is on.
- "Press its button on any page.": beneath it.

- **FR-030** Pipeup for Safari's app window says whether Pipeup is on in Safari, in one line with a drawing, and offers one button: Safari's Extensions settings until it is on, the sample page once it is.

<details><summary>Acceptance criteria (2)</summary>

- **AC-turn-on-in-safari-1** (FR-030): Given Pipeup just installed and not yet ticked in Safari, when the app's window opens, then it reads "Turn on Pipeup in Safari." with "Under Extensions, tick Pipeup." and one button, Open Safari Settings, and nothing else but the drawing and the footer links. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_
- **AC-turn-on-in-safari-2** (FR-030): Given Pipeup ticked under Extensions, when the window is next in front, then it reads "Pipeup is on in Safari." with "Press its button on any page." and the button Try it on a sample page. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_

</details>

### Press Pipeup in the toolbar
![Press Pipeup in the toolbar](../../references/screens/jny-comment-in-safari/press-pipeup--default--desktop--dark.png)

Wording (text the mock does not show as it is; `{…}` is what the data fills in):
- "{address}": the page's host and path; "This page" where Safari gives the extension no address.
- "Click anything on the page to comment on it.": always, with Pipeup off on the page.

- **FR-031** With Pipeup off on the page, the toolbar menu shows the page's address, the one action Comment on this page and one sentence saying what it does, and nothing is added to the page until that action, the shortcut or the right-click item is used.

<details><summary>Acceptance criteria (2)</summary>

- **AC-press-pipeup-1** (FR-031): Given a page without Pipeup, when Maya presses the toolbar button, then the menu shows the address, Comment on this page and "Click anything on the page to comment on it.", with no switch, shortcut or link. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_
- **AC-press-pipeup-2** (FR-031): Given the menu open, when she closes it without choosing, then nothing of Pipeup's is on the page. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_

</details>

### Answer Safari's one question
![Answer Safari's one question](../../references/screens/jny-comment-in-safari/allow-once--default--desktop--dark.png)

Wording (text the mock does not show as it is; `{…}` is what the data fills in):
- "Click anything to comment · Esc when you're done": comment mode's first-run hint in the extension, which names no button on the page.

- **FR-032** In Safari the first use asks, once, whether Pipeup may see websites; the press is never lost, so comment mode starts as soon as the question is answered, and no other question is ever asked for commenting.

<details><summary>Acceptance criteria (2)</summary>

- **AC-allow-once-1** (FR-032): Given a fresh install, when Maya presses Comment on this page, then Safari's sheet shows and, after Always Allow on Every Website, comment mode is on with the hint showing and the badge reading "on", with no second press. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_
- **AC-allow-once-2** (FR-032): Given the question answered with Always Allow on Every Website, when she presses Comment on this page on another site, then no sheet shows. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_

</details>

### Write the first comment
![Write the first comment](../../references/screens/jny-comment-in-safari/first-comment--default--desktop--dark.png)

Wording (text the mock does not show as it is; `{…}` is what the data fills in):
- "Saved in this browser. Press Pipeup in the toolbar to copy, save or send them.": once, after the reviewer's first comment in this browser; the menu's own verbs, said when they are true.

- **FR-033** The first comment is written on the page as on any page with Pipeup, kept by the extension in this browser, and followed once by one line saying where it went and that the toolbar menu copies, saves or sends it.

<details><summary>Acceptance criteria (2)</summary>

- **AC-first-comment-1** (FR-033): Given comment mode on, when Maya clicks the paragraph, types and presses Enter, then the compact card sits beside the paragraph, the badge reads 1 and the line "Saved in this browser. Press Pipeup in the toolbar to copy, save or send them." shows once. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_
- **AC-first-comment-2** (FR-033): Given a second comment written later in the same browser, when it is sent, then no such line shows. _(not tested in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_

</details>

### Copy or save from the toolbar menu
![Copy or save from the toolbar menu](../../references/screens/jny-comment-in-safari/the-menu--default--desktop--dark.png)

Wording (text the mock does not show as it is; `{…}` is what the data fills in):
- "Your comments on this page · {n}": the count of open comments on the page.
- "Copy comments · to paste anywhere": always; after the press it reads "Copied" for a moment.
- "Always on for this site": under More, on any site.
- "Always on for local pages": in its place on localhost and 127.0.0.1, any port.

- **FR-034** With Pipeup on, the toolbar menu is the one menu: the name, Your comments on this page with the count, Copy comments in one press, Save as a file (a Markdown file or a Pipeup file), Commenting with its shortcut, and More for preferences and the way out; Safari leaves out Send to my agent and Keep comments beside the page.

<details><summary>Acceptance criteria (2)</summary>

- **AC-the-menu-1** (FR-034): Given one comment on the page, when Maya presses the toolbar button, then the menu shows Add your name, Your comments on this page · 1, Copy comments · to paste anywhere, Save as a file, Commenting with ⇧⌥C, and More, in that order, with no status line and no footer. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_
- **AC-the-menu-2** (FR-034): Given the menu, when she presses Save as a file, then A Markdown file and A Pipeup file open beneath it, and choosing one saves it where Safari saves downloads. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_

</details>

### A page with Pipeup built in
![A page with Pipeup built in](../../references/screens/jny-comment-in-safari/built-in-page--default--desktop--dark.png)

- **FR-035** On a page with Pipeup built in, the extension adds nothing, its menu says to comment with the page's own button or the shortcut, and the shortcut and the right-click item go to the page's own Pipeup.

<details><summary>Acceptance criteria (2)</summary>

- **AC-built-in-page-1** (FR-035): Given a page with Pipeup built in, when Maya presses the toolbar button, then the menu says the page has Pipeup built in and offers no Comment on this page, and the page's own corner control is untouched. _(proven in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_
- **AC-built-in-page-2** (FR-035): Given that page, when she presses ⇧⌥C, then the page's own Pipeup starts comment mode and the extension adds nothing. _(not tested in the prototype, 2026-11-26)_

</details>
